enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . notes: Wind/gust ranges: quantile-boosted models widened by a conformal margin fit on out-of-fold errors (days 1-10 ensemble model).

Temperature ranges: NBM high/low plus the empirical error distribution (by lead day and season) measured at Alamogordo, Holloman and Las Cruces airports; the same error spread is assumed at Hawk St, the Pass and Cloudcroft (mountain sites are not verified).
Rain: percentile amounts come from the hurdle model; coverage above nominal mostly reflects the large share of dry days. Cloudcroft days 8-10 slightly under-cover (88% vs 90%).
Test period: Jul 2025 – Oct 2026 (about 15 months), so coverage numbers carry a few points of sampling noise.

Updated at 449 PM MST Sat Nov 14 2026

 - Cool and blustery this afternoon, with winds gusting 30 to 40

 - Otherwise, quiet weather looks to prevail next week.

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1216 PM MST Sat Nov 14 2026

It's a cool and blustery day across the region in the wake of last
night's system. The whole area remains under cyclonic flow aloft
as an upper level trough rolls across northern New Mexico. This is
leading to west winds gusting 30 to 35 mph across the area, and
the odd gust to 40 is possible before sunset. Mountain wave clouds
are bringing partly cloudy skies to the lowlands, with more
extensive orographic cloud cover over the higher terrain of the
Gila region and the Sacramento Mountains. A few light showers have
been cropping up as expected, and a few snow flakes have been
spotted around Cloudcroft, where temperatures are in the mid-30s
this afternoon.

West winds will east up tonight as the pressure gradient weakens,
and skies clear out. Patchy fog is possible in some of the more
sheltered valleys. Elsewhere, we'll have just enough wind to
prevent more widespread fog formation. Temperatures will drop into
the upper-30s in some of the sheltered valleys as well. 

Expect less cloud cover and wind on Sunday, with temperatures
climbing a little warmer in the higher terrain. Calmer conditions
Sunday night will allow temperatures to fall deeper into the 30s
in the usual cooler spots in the lowland deserts, with mid to
upper-30s possible in the lowest-lying portions of the Mesilla
Valley. We could push the freezing mark at Jornada Range. 

Easterly flow will keep temperatures at or slightly below normal
early next week, with a warm up late-week allowing highs to
approach the lower-70s.

&&

.AVIATION...
(00Z TAFS)
Issued at 449 PM MST Sat Nov 14 2026

Lots of clouds today and even a few light rain showers. The rain
showers are wrapping up, but we will continue to see some off and
on ceilings of SCT-BKN050-080. By late Sunday morning the ceilings
and most of the clouds will be gone. Currently the all the TAF
sites have low end gusty winds, but I expect those wind gusts to
drop off a few hours after sunset. We will continue to see
generally westerly winds tonight and then winds will be light from
the west or light and variable for Sunday afternoon.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 1216 PM MST Sat Nov 14 2026

Gusty west winds of around 30 to 40 mph this afternoon, but with
high RH and recent rainfall, there are no fire weather concerns.

Near to slightly below normal temperatures and excellent overnight
RH recovery is expected the next several days. Some patchy fog
will be possible in sheltered valleys. 

Vent rates are excellent today with the windy conditions, but will
become far less favorable Sunday into Monday, with some
improvement from Tuesday.
